clue.text: Crummy local's barring Vlad, initially reassuring everyone there

indicators.note: crummy means shoddy or poorly made, so the pub word is knocked into a worse order
a bar blocks a way through, so the jumbled letters stand on either side of what they shut in
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the pub word with its apostrophe dropped
Vlad is the setter, who refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A setter pictures a grotty pub that turns him away while welcoming every other customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled pub word, ALLCOS, holds ME plus the R, giving ALL-COMERS. Vlad is this puzzle's setter, so he is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: All-comers are anyone at all who turns up, so the term covers every person present.

clue.text: Current strength of army regulars' anger over exercises?

indicators.note: regulars are letters taken at even intervals, here every other one of the army word
in a down entry the anger word sits on top of, and so after, the exercises abbreviation when read upward

explanation.surface: Soldiers' fury after drill is gauged as if it were an electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface pun: angry soldiers measured like a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the size of an electric flow measured in amps, i.e. how strong that flow is.

clue.text: Personal generator – 50 per cent reduction for cash upfront

indicators.note: upfront points to the very first letter of the money word as the one being swapped out

blocks.note: halve 100, Roman C, and you get 50, Roman L
cash in the form of coins

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a home generator offering half price to anyone paying up front.
explanation.walkthrough: The C of COINS is the Roman 100; cutting it by half leaves L, the Roman 50, giving LOINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The loins are traditionally the seat of procreative power, the body's own begetting organs.

clue.text: From here? Yes and no

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about where something comes from
setter's reading: the phrase means both superb, an emphatic yes, and literally not from this planet, a no

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase answers both ways: as praise it says yes, wonderful; taken literally it says no, from somewhere beyond Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of this world is an idiom for marvellous, while its literal sense is extraterrestrial, not belonging here.

clue.text: Nurse playing with Rampant Rod underneath blanket

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up on hind legs, so in a down entry the rod word stands upside down

blocks.note: v for versus, as in one team playing another

explanation.surface: A racy scene of a nurse and a man called Rod under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name but is just a pole. 'Underneath' tells you the wordplay sits below the definition in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap or cover completely, as a blanket covers what it lies over.

clue.text: Lesbian in a quiet pub? There's no mistake about it

indicators.note: about means going around, so the no-mistake word wraps the little pub phrase

blocks.note: sic is printed to say a quoted error is genuine, not a mistake
p for piano, quietly in music
PH, public house, as on maps

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted in a quiet bar, and the speaker insists there is no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is the Latin tag editors use to mark an error as the original's, so 'there's no mistake about it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho, the poet of Lesbos, wrote of love between women, so sapphic means lesbian.

clue.text: On the way back catch police agent?

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings, a fishing catch

explanation.surface: On the return journey, someone hopes to nab an undercover officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is an old Scottish measure of landed herring, about 750 fish, so it is a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics officer, a police agent working against drug dealing.

clue.text: Stars in capital stopping with lawyer

indicators.note: stopping here means plugging a gap, so the city sits inside the other words like a cork

blocks.note: DA is an American district attorney

explanation.surface: Celebrities in a capital city halt their travels alongside their attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars looks like celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a group of stars, and also the galaxy that lies in it.

clue.text: Maybe invoked when wanting to 14, it can be big or hard

definitions.text: it can be big or hard

blocks.note: first meaning: the word a photographer tells people to say to make them smile; 14 is the photography answer at 14-across

blocks.clueFragment: it can be big or hard
blocks.note: second meaning: the word follows both big, an important person, and hard, tough luck

explanation.walkthrough: 14-across means to take a photo here. The second half works by completing the phrases big ___ and hard ___.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to say the dairy word to smile, and the same word completes idioms for a bigwig and bad luck.

clue.text: Ability to get through to ancestral suite improved

indicators.note: something improved has been reworked, so these letters are rebuilt into a better order

explanation.surface: Renovating an old family suite of rooms is somehow meant to make you able to reach someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being articulate means expressing yourself clearly, which is the knack of making others understand you.

clue.text: Local favourite keeps old place in field

indicators.note: keeps means holds on to, so the drink word holds the old letter inside it

blocks.note: a pint is the favourite order at the local pub
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A popular figure in the area holds on to an old spot in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, the local is your neighbourhood pub. Point is a fielding position in cricket, near the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Point is a cricket fielding position, so it is a location on the playing area.

clue.text: Following assault, I've repaid family of biters

indicators.note: after an assault things are knocked about and scattered, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone says that after being attacked they have settled the score in kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Viperidae is the zoological family of vipers, venomous snakes that strike with fangs.

clue.text: Still in fluster, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word could be some other version of itself, so its letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remains flustered, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: Still reads as 'yet', but it is an adjective meaning calm, the opposite of fluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful describes calm and quiet, like something still and undisturbed.

clue.text: What about institute? Sense it's awful

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the questioning word is read from right to left

blocks.note: eh, said when you didn't catch something
I is an abbreviation for institute

explanation.surface: Someone questions an institution and senses that it is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Nous is a British informal word for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means utterly wicked or shocking, an intensified sense of very bad.

clue.text: See clearly and shoot

blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: capture a photograph

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the phrase read literally, obtaining a photo by shooting it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grasp a situation, while its literal sense is taking a photo.

clue.text: Picked up kitchen appliance in Northamptonshire town

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so we want a word that is spoken like the appliance

explanation.surface: Someone collected a kitchen gadget while in a Midlands market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Towcester, a small town in Northamptonshire in the English Midlands, is pronounced like the appliance despite its spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Towcester is a market town in Northamptonshire, known for its racecourse.

clue.text: Handyman carrying extra weight round middle, Charlie admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the Charlie letter goes inside the weight word

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
tum is a casual word for the belly or midriff

explanation.surface: A handyman with a paunch round his waist lets a man called Charlie in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a beer belly, but extra weight, round and middle each give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, a general helper or odd-job man.

clue.text: Trash new areas developing in African territory

indicators.note: developing means changing shape over time, so these letters are reformed into something new

explanation.surface: A complaint that newly built-up zones are being spoiled in an African land.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Sahara is a disputed region on the Atlantic coast of north-west Africa.

clue.text: Before end of Games, observe cycling recruits

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so letters at one end of the watch word move to the other end
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the sports word is kept

explanation.surface: Before the Games end, someone watches the new joiners out on their bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling here is not bike riding: it moves the closing letters of a word round to its front without otherwise disturbing the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlists is a verb meaning signs up or engages people, especially for military service.

clue.text: Not in practice, I'm soon about to climb league

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for soon goes around the short phrase
climbing in a down entry means going upward, so the combined letters are read bottom to top

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
L is an abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: Someone says they will soon move up a sports league, though it is not happening yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means existing in name only, so something nominal does not operate in reality.

clue.text: Snoopers having second period of inactivity

blocks.note: the Stasi were the East German secret police, notorious for spying on citizens
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Spies are given a second spell of doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill, where nothing moves or develops.

clue.text: Plant official in work

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, so the official sits within the labour word

explanation.surface: An insider is planted in a workplace as a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant could be a verb or a spy; here it is the green kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is a clover-like plant with three-lobed leaves, such as bird's-foot trefoil.

clue.text: Film star nuts about female either way

indicators.note: either way means the word reads the same forwards and backwards
about means around, so the nuts word goes round the female word

blocks.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak trees

explanation.surface: A movie star is crazy about women, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuts reads as crazy, but it is the noun: mast, the nuts that beech trees drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was a Hollywood actress of the 1930s famous for her innuendo-laden lines.

clue.text: Not a reason to show up one of 9

indicators.note: to show means put on view, so the letters are already on display inside the phrase
up in a down entry means going from bottom to top, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: spanning the three words, starting in the first

explanation.surface: Some argument is said to be no reason to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is not a cross-reference here: it is nine, the number of the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of love poetry, one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.

clue.text: Starts to feel comfortable on bench? Wrong

blocks.note: a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Someone begins to relax on a bench, then finds it is the wrong thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle in is to become used to new surroundings and grow at ease.

clue.text: Pass stick over teacher's head

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the stick word is flipped and read from right to left
the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the teacher word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone hands a cane over the teacher's head, as in an old-fashioned classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a law is to make it into law, and enact is the formal verb for that.

clue.text: Yes, take action to keep Republican in check

indicators.note: to keep means to hold, so the legal action word holds the party letter inside it
in check means held back or restrained, reinforcing that the party letter is held captive inside

explanation.surface: An agreement to bring a lawsuit to restrain a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure is an informal way of agreeing, an equivalent of certainly or OK.

clue.text: Lots here, also some jumping over side

indicators.note: jumping means leaping about, so these letters hop around into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd scene where several people are hopping over a barrier at the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Lots means many, but here it is items for sale at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesroom is an auction room, where items are put up for sale as numbered lots.
